items.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: My early incarnation of the Catatonic Five played mostly on the campus. We occasionally played at other colleges. We played at Union on one occasion and this is an example of how the alcohol situation got out of control. Dave Barbour was the pianist and he needed to read music.

ctx.x: Right. Well Phil described some of the going out on weekends and playing on other campuses. I assume you guys did the same thing?

Yes but not to the same extent that the second incarnation of the Catatonic Five. My early incarnation of the Catatonic Five played mostly on the campus. We occasionally played at other colleges. We played at Union on one occasion and this is an example of how the alcohol situation got out of control. Dave Barbour was the pianist and he needed to read music. And our alcoholic consumption had got to a stage where it seemed to be a good idea, since we were playing out on the front lawn of this fraternity house, to…
was the wrong thing to do, and we had to flee and the police came after us but they never caught us. But anyway.
